description: The USGS National Strong Motion Project, or NSMP, has outfitted more than 250 structures across the United States with seismic sensors, and its page on earthquake monitoring of structures explains what the recordings are for. After a damaging earthquake, recordings help engineers assess a building's safety quickly; they also show how structural and nonstructural parts such as equipment and pipes are damaged by shaking, and support better earthquake-resistant design, prediction of seismic performance and code provisions. Examples on the page are the recently retrofitted seven-storey main hospital building at the San Diego VA Medical Center, with sensors from basement to roof and a triaxial sensor on the ground floor, structural health monitoring of Veterans Affairs hospital buildings, the UNLV Environmentally Friendly Science and Engineering Building, and animations of how the Atwood and Frontier buildings in Anchorage shook in the M7.1 earthquake of 24 January 2016. Coverage: US instrumented buildings, including hospitals. Access: the page links to NSMP data, station map and structural array pages, which were not read; no licence is stated on it. Useful for seismic vulnerability and structural response models of buildings and hospitals; related records are not yet linked.
